name: Question 2
problem: For which of the following vector fields is $f(x,y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x-3y)$ a potential function?
worked_solution:
A vector field $F$ is conservative if it is the gradient of a scalar function $f.$ That is, there exists a function $f$ such that $F=∇f.$ The function $f$ is called a potential function for $F.$

To compute the vector field associated with a potential function $f,$ we compute its gradient.

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\,i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x-3y))\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x-3y))\,j \\  & =4\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x-3y)\,i-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x-3y)\,j \\  & =F\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector field that has $f$ as a potential function is

$$
F=4\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x-3y)\,i-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x-3y)\,j.
$$

Question 2
?

For which of the following vector fields is f(x,y)=sin⁡(4x−3y) a potential function?

a
−4cos⁡(4x−3y)i−3sin⁡(4x−3y)j
b
3cos⁡(4x−3y)i−4sin⁡(4x−3y)j
c
4cos⁡(4x−3y)i−3cos⁡(4x−3y)j
d
4cos⁡(4x−3y)i+3cos⁡(4x−3y)j
e
−3sin⁡(4x−3y)i+4cos⁡(4x−3y)j
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A vector field F is conservative if it is the gradient of a scalar function f. That is, there exists a function f such that F=∇f. The function f is called a potential function for F.

To compute the vector field associated with a potential function f, we compute its gradient. ∇f=∂f∂xi+∂f∂yj=∂∂x(sin⁡(4x−3y))i+∂∂y(sin⁡(4x−3y))j=4cos⁡(4x−3y)i−3cos⁡(4x−3y)j=F

Therefore, the vector field that has f as a potential function is F=4cos⁡(4x−3y)i−3cos⁡(4x−3y)j.
